article_title: GitHub Desktop Adds Multi-Account Support Per Host, Letting Developers Keep Work and Personal Logins Signed In Together

content_preview.title: GitHub Desktop Adds Multi-Account Support Per Host, Letting Developers Keep Work and Personal Logins Signed In Together
content_preview.summary: GitHub Desktop 3.7.0 lets users sign in with more than one account on the same host and assign a GitHub account per repository, after the feature spent weeks in beta.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

GitHub has added support for signing in with more than one account on the same host in GitHub Desktop, its graphical Git client. According to the [GitHub Changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-11-19-github-desktop-now-supports-multiple-accounts-per-host/), "GitHub Desktop now lets you sign in with more than one account on the same host, including GitHub.com, GitHub Enterprise Server, and GHE.com." editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News article (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis). 781 words, within the 400-1200 News range. Neutral, descriptive tone throughout; no sensationalism or editorializing. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200, no archive_fallback, suspicious_patterns: null on every entry) and sha256-verified by decompressing each .html.gz and recomputing the hash against manifest.json: source-0 (c162f5cd...) = github.blog/changelog 2026-11-19 multi-account post; source-1 (87a85c76...) = github.blog/changelog 2026-11-02 short-lived-tokens post; source-2 (761a7170...) = github.com/desktop/desktop/releases. Read the extracted plain text of all three snapshots in full (not just the manifest excerpt). Performed a literal quote-by-quote audit: every double-quoted string in the article body ('GitHub Desktop now lets you sign in with more than one account...', 'Add more than one account for a single host, with no fixed limit,', 'Associate each repository with a specific account...', "Change a repository's account association at any time...", 'Choose an account' / 'infer it when only one can', 'Existing repositories are migrated automatically...', 'download the latest (GitHub Desktop 3.7.0)', 'When you sign in to GitHub Desktop 3.6.10 or later...', 'Short-lived access tokens reduce how long a leaked token can be used.', 'automatically refreshes them for GitHub API requests and Git operations...', 'rolling this out gradually on github.com...', "This token rollout doesn't include GitHub Enterprise Server.", 'Work with personal and work accounts side by side without signing out...', "Choose the account used for each repository's GitHub access and HTTPS authentication...", 'Repositories are grouped by their assigned account when multiple GitHub accounts are used on the same host.', 'Use short-lived tokens for new logged-in users') is a verbatim substring of its cited snapshot, case and punctuation included (only curly vs. straight apostrophes differ, which is expected markdown rendering, not a case/wording mismatch). No case-mismatch or paraphrase-as-quote issues found in the submitted text. Version/date pairs checked directly against source-2's release list: 3.6.11-beta1 = 03 Nov 14:29 (correct), 3.6.12-beta2 = 16 Nov 16:18 (correct), 3.6.8 = 02 Nov 12:59 (correct, matches the short-lived-tokens code change quote). Confirmed the 'What We Don't Know' version-gap caveat is accurate: source-2's visible release list (page 1 of the releases feed, fetched same day as this review) runs only through 3.6.12-beta2/3.6.11 and contains no itemized 3.7.0 entry, so the claim that 3.7.0's description comes from the changelog post rather than a release-notes entry holds. Checked the submission body and all three raw snapshots for the GitHub issue reference '#3707' and for any description of GitHub Desktop as 'free' -- neither appears anywhere in the submitted article or in any of the three sources (the only 'free' hits in source-0/source-1 are unrelated nav boilerplate, 'Use Copilot for free'); this confirms the writer's self-reported removal of the hallucinated issue number and the unsourced 'free' descriptor left no residue in the final text. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is a GitHub Desktop feature; Anthropic/Claude appears only as contributor_model metadata, not in the headline, summary, lead, or as a credited passage.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No unsourced claims, no hallucinated specifics. The one inferential claim not in quote marks -- 'GitHub Desktop could only hold one signed-in identity per host' -- is a fair paraphrase of the changelog's framing ('now lets you sign in with more than one account', 'one of the most requested features') and is reasonable context, not an unsupported fact. Absence/quantifier language ('no fixed limit', 'does not say whether... rolling out gradually', 'had not yet published a dedicated, itemized changelog entry') was checked against all three sources and holds up; none of it claims something stronger than what the sources omit.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; headline and summary are descriptive, not promotional. No loaded language.
